_comment: Astro Next network endpoint manifest — issue #10.
HAND-MAINTAINED JUDGEMENT ONLY. The host set is not typed here: it is derived on every
run by tools/policy/endpoint_seed.py, which imports issue #6's
tools/baseline/inventory_endpoints.py and adds a scan of webui/ that generator does not
perform. tools/policy/manifest.py joins the two STRICTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so a host
that appears in committed text without an entry here fails, and an entry naming a host
nothing references fails unless it says why it cannot be derived.
Schema: endpoint-manifest.schema.json. State vocabulary: README.md.
THIS IS NOT A MEASURED TRACE. It is what the source says. Every field reading
`not-captured` names something a running browser behind a recorder would answer;
tools/baseline/capture-network.sh is that harness and refuses to emit a trace it did
not record. It is blocked until an Astro binary exists (baseline finding 1).
THE LIST IS EMPTY. Every patch in both declared series applies, in declared order,
at the locked Chromium revision: 112 ungoogled and 56 Astro, 168 of 168. No host a
patch ADDS is missing from a patched tree for want of the patch applying, and no
entry below may cite a non-applying patch as the reason for its observed_state.
MEASURED, not declared. The measurement replays BOTH series in declared order
against a scratch tree holding the pristine version of every file any patch names,
with git apply --check --whitespace=nowarn as the acceptance test -- the same test
apply-patches.sh uses. No fuzz, no --3way, no --recount. The replay reads its
pristine input from TWO places: chromium/src records 13 of the files the series
touches inside gclient-fetched DEPS subrepos, as gitlinks (third_party/devtools-
frontend/src, third_party/search_engines_data/resources), so git show HEAD:<path>
cannot read them; those paths are resolved from the SUBREPO's own git at exactly
the commit the gitlink records -- pristine by construction, and unaffected by the
edits an earlier apply run left in the subrepo working trees.
How the list emptied, in three waves, all of them the same defect:
76466c6  045, 046, 052, 053 and 056 had hunk headers whose line counts
disagreed with their bodies. git apply calls that a corrupt patch and
rejects it against any tree at all, so these had never applied anywhere.
Four had drifted as well and were re-anchored.
3310e14  020, 023, 027, 036 and 039 had each been generated by diffing an
already-ungoogled tree against pristine, so each carried edits belonging
to an ungoogled patch or to domain substitution as though they were
Astro's own. Slimmed to the Astro-specific intent. The same commit
corrected the replay's gitlink blindness, which cleared all eight
reported ungoogled failures -- they had ONE root cause, fix-building-
with-prunned-binaries naming a devtools-frontend file, so that patch was
skipped whole and four later ungoogled patches failed on edits it never
made -- and moved 009, 012, 013 and 015 the other way, onto this list.
THIS     009, 012, 013 and 015, the last four, have the same origin as the
second wave: all four apply to the PRISTINE file, which is what proves
they were diffed against an already-ungoogled tree. 009 and 013 had
adopted remove-uneeded-ui's deletion of three <ph>Learn more</ph> help
links each; 012 its rewrite of the settings subpage help button to
if=[[false]]; 015 the three profile_menu_view.cc edits belonging to
remove-unused-preferences-fields. Each is regenerated as the difference
between the in-series base and the original patch's own result, so what
remains is the Astro intent alone and nothing is authored by hand.
Coupling this created, measured by skipping the collider rather than reasoned:
only 009 now REQUIRES remove-uneeded-ui (its three renames land on lines that
patch rewrites). 012, 013 and 015 apply with or without their former collider. No
Astro patch is coupled to another by this change: of the five files involved, one
has no other writer at all and each of the other four has exactly one Astro writer
and one ungoogled writer.
The validator's limit, which an empty list makes sharper rather than milder: the
rule here checks only that each name is in patches/astro/series, so with nothing
named it now examines ZERO entries and cannot fail. It never could detect a change
of apply status. What keeps this list honest is the replay above, which needs a
Chromium checkout and which this module deliberately does not run.

hosts.rationale: Oxy Identity's authorisation host. REPLACE, not KEEP: the current flow returns access_token and refresh_token as URL query parameters (src/chrome/browser/oxy/oxy_auth_callback_handler.cc:31-32), which the epic forbids outright. #16 rebuilds it on Authorization Code + PKCE, which changes the request shape at this host.
hosts.trigger: user starts sign-in from the profile menu
hosts.response_purpose: establish an Oxy session for the profile
hosts.user_control: signing in is user-initiated; no request before first sign-in
hosts.blocks_reason: The callback is astro://auth/callback (src/chrome/browser/oxy/oxy_auth_service.h:22-23). May a REMOTE origin navigate to the trusted scheme? Decided: no — and the mechanism that would enforce it does not exist yet. content::IsSafeRedirectTarget (content/public/common/url_utils.cc:81-107) rejects a privileged redirect target through HasWebUIScheme at :95, and that reads a three-element literal at :27-31 which does not contain `astro`; `astro` is not in kUnsafeSchemes at :82-94 either, so the function returns true and content/browser/loader/navigation_url_loader_impl.cc:1575-1577 raises no net::ERR_UNSAFE_REDIRECT. Any HTTPS origin could therefore 302 into astro://auth/callback with attacker-chosen query parameters. #11 milestone 1 ships no auth host, so registration is not blocked; shipping any credential-consuming host on astro:// is, until IsWebUIScheme is generalised. See the oxy-identity feature entry for the full statement.
hosts.notes: oxy_cookie_signin_observer.cc:28 watches a cookie named `fedcm_session`. The Oxy platform's own instructions record FedCM and the fedcm_session cookie as deleted ecosystem-wide in the 2026-07 device-first migration. Declared, not measured here. NOT_BUILT: baseline finding 1 — nothing links src/chrome/browser/oxy into the build graph, so no binary built from committed source contains this code. That is a build defect owned by #7, not a disposition.

hosts.rationale: DoH template offered by Astro settings — Cloudflare, and the DEFAULT (sections.ts:192). The settings handler maps this to the real Chromium prefs `dns_over_https.mode` and `dns_over_https.templates` (src/chrome/browser/oxy/webui/astro_settings_handler.cc:64-65), so a shipped default sends every DNS query the browser makes to one third party.

investigate.question: Does Astro ship a DoH provider ON by default, and if so which? The settings UI offers Cloudflare as the default value, but whether `dns_over_https.mode` is `secure`/`automatic` out of the box is not established, and the difference is between 'no default DNS provider' and 'every lookup goes to Cloudflare'.
investigate.answered_by: Read the registered default for `dns_over_https.mode` in the built profile, then decide as part of #20's transport-security baseline. Astro registers no default for it in the committed patch stack — 020-register-oxy-prefs.patch does not appear in docs/astro-next/baseline/pref-dispositions.json for these keys.

The inherited iridium patch `all-add-trk-prefixes-to-possibly-evil-connections.patch` rewrites the URL literal to `trk:NNN:https://…`, and `block-trk-and-subdomains.patch` makes `trk:` unresolvable (components/url_formatter/url_fixer.cc returns an empty GURL). So the host appears on BOTH diff sides: the literal survives, the request cannot. That is DISABLE_RUNTIME as an observed state — the calling code is still compiled and reachable — which is why it may never be asserted as 'cannot happen'.

hosts.rationale: The New Tab Page's weather widget (webui/ntp/src/main.ts:430). Unreachable in the shipped context by TWO independent mechanisms, both named: the page's own isWebUIContext() guard returns before the fetch (main.ts:424-427), and astro_ntp_ui.cc sets no connect-src, so the WebUI default-src blocks it anyway. It is live in the Vite dev server. DORMANT, not DISABLE_RUNTIME: nobody decided to switch it off — the code was written and the surrounding arrangement happens to stop it, which is exactly the state that becomes reachable again when someone relaxes a CSP for an unrelated reason.
